prereg.question: on CIC-IoMT-2024, with nine seeds instead of three, does a pruned and recovered detector raise unseen reconnaissance less often, more often, or as often as the dense detector trained and recovered the same way, at matched in-distribution risk
prereg.motivation: notebook 47 (three seeds): Fisher students raised unseen reconnaissance less on every seed (shallow 9.2% vs 22.7%, deep 19.5% vs 51.5%), magnitude students less on two seeds of three, no interval excluding zero; on CICIoT2023 (notebook 41, five seeds) the magnitude students raised it more on both networks

design.protocol: notebook 47 unchanged: same bridge, Setting construction, teacher training, acceptance rule, dense reference, scoring, prefix calibration, recovery, recalibration and audit
design.pooling: notebook 47's reconnaissance rows (seeds 101, 211, 307) plus this notebook's rows; paired by seed; nine seeds per network and rule
design.acceptance_rule: notebook 47's: benign escalation <= 0.15, attack recall >= 0.85, fine macro-F1 >= 0.40 on the remaining classes after recalibration; failing cells excluded and listed

readings.less: per network and rule: the paired gap (dense minus student, share raised as attack) is at least 0.05 with its 95% interval above zero and the cell is matched (mean paired in-distribution HSR difference within 0.02): the student raises the family less
readings.more: per network and rule: the paired gap is negative with its 95% interval below zero: the student raises the family more
readings.level: neither: the interval contains zero or the mean is below 0.05
readings.per_network: pruned_raise_less if both rules read less; pruned_raise_more if both read more; mixed otherwise

expectation.Z1: the Fisher student reads 'less' on at least one network (the three-seed direction holds)

prereg.reporting_rule: every cell reported as measured; whichever way it reads, Section V of the paper states it
